			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Item 1. Business:<a name="Item1Business_899345"></a></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">The Company</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Calgon Carbon Corporation (the Company) is a global leader in innovative solutions, high quality products and reliable services designed to protect human health and the environment from harmful contaminants in water, and air.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a leading manufacturer of activated carbon, with broad capabilities in ultraviolet light disinfection, the Company provides purification solutions for drinking water, wastewater, pollution abatement, and a variety of industrial and commercial manufacturing processes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On November 2, 2016, the Company completed the acquisition of the wood-based activated carbon, reactivation and mineral-based filtration media business of CECA, a subsidiary of Arkema Group (New Business).&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to the complementary nature of the New Business&#x2019; products and market applications to those of the Company, and its significant exposure to less regulated, more traditional end markets, the addition of the New Business to the Company creates a more balanced global platform from which the Company can continue to grow by leveraging its now expanded capabilities in the global activated carbon and adjacent filtration media market areas.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company was organized as a Delaware corporation in 1967.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Products and Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company offers a diverse range of products, services, and equipment specifically developed for the purification, separation, and concentration, and filtration of liquids, gases, and other media through its reportable business segments:&nbsp;&nbsp;Activated Carbon and Service, Equipment, Consumer, and Other.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2016, Other is exclusively comprised of the results of the New Business. </font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>

			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Activated Carbon and Service segment manufactures and markets granular and powdered activated carbon for use in many distinct market applications that remove organic compounds from water, air, and other liquids and gases.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Service aspect of this segment consists of carbon reactivation and the leasing, installation, monitoring and maintenance of carbon adsorption equipment.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">

			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Equipment segment provides solutions to customers&#x2019; air, water and other liquid purification problems through the design, fabrication, installation and sale of equipment systems that utilize one or more of the Company&#x2019;s enabling technologies: carbon adsorption, ultraviolet (UV) light (for ballast water, drinking water, and wastewater treatment), and advanced ion-exchange (IX) technologies.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Consumer segment supplies activated carbon cloth for use in medical, military, and industrial applications.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The New Business, reported in Other, manufactures and markets granular and powdered wood-based activated carbon, coal-based activated carbon reactivation, diatomaceous earth and perlite filtration media for use in various distinct market applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;They are used primarily for decolorization, purification, decontamination, and filtration of liquids in various applications including food and beverage, industrial, fine chemicals and pharmaceuticals.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For further information, refer to Note 18 to the consolidated financial statements in Item 8 of this Annual Report.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Activated Carbon and Service.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;The sale of activated carbon is the principal component of the Activated Carbon and Service business segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is recognized as the leading manufacturer of bituminous coal-based granular activated carbon.&nbsp;&nbsp;Activated carbon is a porous material that removes organic compounds from liquids and gases by a process known as &#x201C;adsorption.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;In adsorption, undesirable organic molecules contained in a liquid or gas are attracted and bound to the surface of the pores of the activated carbon as the liquid or gas is passed through.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The primary raw material used in the production of the Company&#x2019;s activated carbons is bituminous coal, which is crushed, sized and then processed in rotary kilns followed by high temperature furnaces.&nbsp;&nbsp;This heating process is known as &#x201C;activation&#x201D; and develops the pore structure of the carbon.&nbsp;&nbsp;Through adjustments in the activation process, pores of the required size and number are developed for a particular purification application.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s technological expertise in adjusting the pore structure in the activation process has been one of a number of factors enabling the Company to develop many special types of activated carbon available in several particle sizes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also markets activated carbons from other raw materials, including coconut shell and wood.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">4</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Activated Carbon and Service business segment produces and sells a broad range of activated, impregnated or acid washed carbons in granular, powdered or pellet form.&nbsp;&nbsp;Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) particles are irregular in shape and generally used in fixed filter beds for continuous flow purification processes.&nbsp;&nbsp;Powdered Activated Carbon (PAC) is carbon that has been pulverized into powder and is often used in batch purification processes, in municipal water treatment applications and for flue gas emissions control.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pelletized activated carbons are extruded particles, cylindrical in shape, and are typically used for gas phase applications due to the low pressure drop, high mechanical strength, and low dust content of the product.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Another important component of the Activated Carbon and Service business segment is the optional services that the Company makes available to purchasers of its products and systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;It offers a variety of treatment services for customers including carbon supply, equipment leasing, installation and demobilization, transportation, and spent carbon reactivation.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other services include feasibility testing, process design, performance monitoring, and major maintenance of Company-owned adsorption equipment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Spent carbon reactivation and re-supply is a key focus of the Company&#x2019;s service business.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the reactivation process, the spent GAC is subjected to high temperature remanufacturing conditions that destroy the adsorbed organics and ensure that the activated carbon is returned to usable quality.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is permitted to handle and reactivate spent carbons containing hazardous and non-hazardous organic compounds.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Granular carbon reactivation is conducted at numerous locations throughout the world.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is valuable to a customer for both environmental and economic reasons, allowing them to reuse carbon cost-effectively without purchasing more expensive new carbon, and, at the same time, protecting natural resources.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company provides reactivation services in packages ranging from a fifty-five gallon drum to truckload quantities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s custom reactivation process for United States (U.S.) municipal drinking water treatment plants is specially tailored to meet the unique demands of the drinking water industry.&nbsp;&nbsp;Activated carbon reactivation for use in drinking water treatment facilities in the U.S. must adhere to requirements of the American Water Works Association (AWWA) standard B605.&nbsp;&nbsp;Perhaps the most important requirement of this standard is that the reactivator must return to the municipality/water provider its own activated carbon that has been reactivated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unlike industrial activated carbon reactivation practiced by a number of carbon companies, where carbons from different customers can be co-mingled and reactivated as a pooled material, drinking water carbons are carefully segregated.&nbsp;&nbsp;This means that a drinking water provider&#x2019;s activated carbon is kept separate not only from industrial customers&#x2019; carbons, but from the activated carbon of other providers&#x2019; activated carbon as well, to avoid any potential cross-contamination.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company maintains the integrity of each drinking water provider&#x2019;s carbon, and its potable reactivation facilities and procedures strictly adhere to AWWA B605.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s Blue Lake, California, Columbus, Ohio, North Tonawanda, New York, and Gila Bend, Arizona plants have received certification from the National Sanitation Foundation International (NSF) under NSF/ANSI Standard 61: Drinking Water System Components - Health Effects for custom reactivated carbon for potable water applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;NSF International is an independent, not-for-profit organization committed to protecting and improving public health and the environment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">European custom reactivation process maintains the segregation of drinking water provider&#x2019;s activated carbon and ensures returned product fulfills the requirements of European Standard EN12015 as well as specific additional requirements as found in the United Kingdom Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI) approval list of products and in the KIWA-ATA certification.&nbsp;&nbsp;Custom reactivation for European municipal drinking water treatment plants is performed in reactivation facilities in Belgium, the United Kingdom, and Italy.&nbsp;&nbsp;The site in Feluy, Belgium, which is accredited ISO9001 and ISO14001 for Quality and Environmental management systems, is the only carbon reactivation facility in the world with ISO22000 accreditation for Food Safety Management System (FSMS).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Transportation services are offered via bulk activated carbon deliveries and spent carbon returns through the Company&#x2019;s private fleet of trailers, capable of transporting both hazardous and non-hazardous material.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company will arrange transportation for packaged and smaller volumes of activated carbon in appropriate containers and small returnable equipment through a network of commercial and less-than-truckload carriers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Sales for the Activated Carbon and Service segment were $454.6 million, $486.5 million, and $498.2 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2016, 2015, and 2014, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Equipment.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;Along with providing activated carbon products, the Company has developed a portfolio of standardized, pre-engineered, activated carbon adsorption systems&#x2014;for both liquid and vapor applications&#x2014;which can be quickly delivered and easily installed at treatment sites.&nbsp;&nbsp;Liquid phase equipment systems are used for potable water treatment, process purification, wastewater treatment, groundwater remediation, and de-chlorination.&nbsp;&nbsp;Vapor phase equipment systems are used to control volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, off gases from air strippers, and landfill gas production.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Through its UV Technologies LLC subsidiary, the Company also manufactures and sells a broad line of UV (ultraviolet) light disinfection equipment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Following the Company&#x2019;s introduction of an advanced UV oxidation process to remediate contaminated groundwater, in 1998, its scientists invented a UV disinfection process used to inactivate Cryptosporidium, Giardia and other similar pathogens in surface water, rendering them harmless to humans.&nbsp;&nbsp;In combination with hydrogen peroxide, UV light is effective in destroying many contaminants common in groundwater remediation applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company participates in the marketplace for innovative UV technologies with its Sentinel&#xAE; line designed to protect municipal drinking water supplies from&nbsp;pathogens, the C3 Series&#x2122; open-channel wastewater disinfection product line for municipal wastewater disinfection, and Rayox&#xAE;&nbsp;UV advanced oxidation equipment for treatment of contaminants in groundwater, process water, and industrial wastewater. &nbsp; &nbsp;UV oxidation equipment can also be combined with activated carbon to provide effective solutions for taste and odor removal in municipal drinking water and for water reuse.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Under the trade name Hyde Marine, which was acquired in&nbsp;2010, the Company also manufactures and sells UV ballast water management systems (BWMS) that combine filtration and UV disinfection to treat and disinfect the ballast water taken in by a ship in one location, and discharged in another, to prevent the spread of non-indigenous aquatic organisms.&nbsp;&nbsp;Invasion of non-native species via ballast water is considered to be one of the greatest threats to the world&#x2019;s waterways and marine environment. &nbsp; &nbsp;The Company competes in this market with its Hyde GUARDIAN&#xAE; BWMS &#x2013; an easy-to-use, cost-effective, and chemical-free ballast water management solution.&nbsp;&nbsp;The International Maritime Organization (IMO) type approved system meets the needs of ship owners committed to operating their vessels in a responsible, sustainable, and economic way through its proven reliability, flexible and compact design, and low operating costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2017, the Company is planning to complete the testing of its BWMS in order to apply to become type approved by the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) for treating ballast water discharged in U.S. waterways.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company also manufactures and sells fixed bed and continuous ion exchange equipment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The proprietary continuous ISEP&#xAE; (Ionic Separator) and CSEP&#xAE; (Chromatographic Separator) units are used for the purification, separation and recovery of many products in the food and beverage, pharmaceutical, mining, chemical, and biotechnology industries.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ISEP&#xAE; and CSEP&#xAE; systems are currently used in installations worldwide for a variety of applications in industrial settings, as well as in selected environmental applications including perchlorate and nitrate removal from drinking water.&nbsp;&nbsp;The core technology of these systems is the proprietary rotary distribution valve.&nbsp;&nbsp;This valve technology is offered in combination with a turntable for movement of media vessels, or with static media vessels where vessel-movement is simulated by recent advances in valve technology. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company assembles its equipment using parts that are both manufactured internally as well as purchased from other suppliers.&nbsp;&nbsp;During periods of heightened demand, manufacturing and assembly may be outsourced to other qualified manufacturers.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Sales for the Equipment segment were $38.9 million, $39.3 million, and $45.3 million for the years ended December 31, 2016, 2015, and 2014, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Consumer.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;The primary product offered in the Consumer segment is carbon cloth.&nbsp;&nbsp;Carbon cloth, which is activated carbon in cloth form, is manufactured in the United Kingdom (UK) and sold to the medical, military, and specialty markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;First developed in the 1970&#x2019;s, activated carbon cloth was originally used in military clothing and masks to protect wearers against nuclear, biological and chemical agents.&nbsp;&nbsp;Today, activated carbon cloth can be used in numerous additional applications, including sensor protection, filters for ostomy bags, wound dressings, conservation of artifacts, and respiratory masks.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Other.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;As mentioned previously, the Company&#x2019;s New Business is reported in Other.&nbsp;&nbsp;In summary, the New Business is a leading European manufacturer of wood-based activated carbon, coal-based activated carbon reactivation, and diatomaceous earth and perlite filtration media, and a leading distributor of such products and services primarily throughout the European region and into Asia.&nbsp;&nbsp;With four manufacturing facilities located in France and two in Italy, the 2016 sales of the New Business were $12.1 million from its date of acquisition on November 2, 2016 through December 31, 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The New Business&#x2019; wood-based activated carbon manufacturing facility is located in Parentis en Born, France, which is ideally situated in the heart of a forest in Europe.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is the only European activated carbon facility to have both steam and chemical activation process capabilities on the same site.&nbsp;&nbsp;The New Business&#x2019; manufacturing processes impart first-rate physio-chemical properties to the final activated carbon products including high porosity, large adsorption capacity, permeability, and &#x2013; when combined with a washing process &#x2013; a high level of purity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Its products are sold primarily in Europe to food, beverage, industrial, fine chemicals and pharmaceutical customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;It also sells product into Asia, primarily India, principally for pharmaceutical end market usage.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s products are well known in the regional market places as Acticarbone&#xAE; and Anticromos&#xAE;.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The New Business&#x2019; coal-based granular activated carbon reactivation capability is located in northern Italy, which is complementary to the location of the Company&#x2019;s other European reactivation facilities &#x2013; which are located in the UK and Belgium.&nbsp;&nbsp;Its capabilities include both food grade and industrial grade reactivation kilns.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The remainder of the New Business is related to the manufacture of diatomaceous earth (DE) and perlite filtration media products.&nbsp;&nbsp;These products, which are primarily used as filter aids in beverage, food, and industrial applications, are marketed and distributed across the European region in relatively close proximity to their manufacturing locations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For the production of DE products, the New Business is vertically integrated from the raw material source to the final product, as it owns two mineral deposit quarry sources which provide raw materials for its DE manufacturing processes.&nbsp;&nbsp;DE is manufactured from diatomite, which is a lightweight and porous rock formed over many years by the successive accumulation and fossilization of the skeletal remains of single-cell algae &#x2013; or diatoms &#x2013; that lived in lakes, and were able to fix soluble silica on their shells.&nbsp;&nbsp;These owned quarries each have 20 or more years of raw material reserves available.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company manufactures DE through a multi-step process that includes crushing, milling, calcination, and packaging.&nbsp;&nbsp;The New Business&#x2019; DE products are sold throughout the European region under the broadly recognized Clarcel&#xAE; brand name. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The New Business&#x2019; perlite products, widely known in Europe as Randalite&#xAE; and Randafil&#x2122;, are manufactured from perlite oar, which is a silica rock of volcanic origin that contains fine water droplets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Through the New Business&#x2019; manufacturing process it is expanded at high temperature then crushed and grated into final product form.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company obtains its raw material for perlite manufacturing from mines located in the Mediterranean region.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Markets&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company participates in six primary markets:&nbsp;&nbsp;Potable Water, Industrial Process, Environmental Water, Environmental Air, Food and Beverage, and Specialty markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Potable Water applications include municipal drinking water treatment as well as point of entry and point of use devices.&nbsp;&nbsp;Applications in the Industrial Process Market include catalysis, product recovery and purification of chemicals, specialty chemicals and pharmaceuticals, as well as process water treatment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The major applications for the two Environmental markets include wastewater treatment, groundwater remediation, ballast water treatment, VOC removal from vapors, and mercury control in flue gas streams.&nbsp;&nbsp;Food and Beverage applications include wine, bottling, brewing, amino acids, and sweetener purification.&nbsp;&nbsp;Medical, personal protection (military and industrial), automotive, consumer, and precious metals applications comprise the Specialty Market.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Potable Water Market.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;The Company sells activated carbons, equipment, custom reactivation services, ion exchange technology, and UV technologies to municipalities for the treatment of potable water.&nbsp;&nbsp;The activated carbon adsorption technology is used to remove both regulated and non-regulated contaminants of concern, including disinfection by-products precursors, perfluorinated compounds, pesticides, carcinogenic volatile organic compounds, algal toxins, other dissolved organic materials, and taste and odor compounds to meet regulated limits or to make the water quality acceptable to the public.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also sells to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of home water purification systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;Granular and powdered activated carbon products are sold in this market and in many cases the </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">7</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">granular activated carbon functions both as the primary filtration media as well as an adsorption media to remove contaminants from the water.&nbsp;&nbsp;Ion exchange resins are sold for use in both fixed beds and continuous counter-current operations to meet strict regulatory guidelines for perchlorate in water.&nbsp;&nbsp;UV advanced oxidation systems are sold for the destruction of waterborne contaminants, and UV disinfection systems are sold for the inactivation of pathogens in surface water.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Industrial Process Market.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;In industrial processing, the Company&#x2019;s activated carbon and DE filtration media products are used either for purification, separation or concentration of customers&#x2019; products in the manufacturing process.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company sells a wide range of activated carbons to the chemical, petroleum refining, and process industries for the purification of organic and inorganic chemicals, amines and vitamins.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, activated carbon is used in treatment of natural gas, biogas and other high purity gases to remove unwanted contamination.&nbsp;&nbsp;The liquefied natural gas industry uses activated carbons to remove mercury compounds that would otherwise corrode process equipment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Activated carbons are also sold for gasoline vapor recovery equipment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has a range of high purity activated carbons that are ideally suited as catalyst carriers and for use in the fine chemicals and pharmaceutical industries.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s advanced ion exchange technology is used for a variety of industrial processes including separation and recovery in hydrometallurgy applications, decolorization in pulp and paper, the production of organic and inorganic chemicals, and the purification of brine.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Environmental Water and Air Markets.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;The Company offers its products and services to assist various industries in meeting the stringent environmental requirements imposed by various government entities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Products used for wastewater and ballast water treatment, the cleanup of contaminated groundwater, surface impoundments, and accidental spills comprise a significant need in this market.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company provides products and services employing both activated carbon adsorption and UV technologies for emergency and temporary cleanup services as well as for permanent installations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s reactivation service is an especially important element if the customer has contaminants that are hazardous organic chemicals.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reactivation of spent carbon protects the environment and eliminates the customers&#x2019; expense, potential liability, and difficulty in securing disposal options (such as landfills) for hazardous organic chemicals.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">Activated carbon is also used in the chemical, pharmaceutical, and refining industries for purification of air discharge to remove contaminants such as benzene, toluene, and other volatile organics.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, reduction of mercury emissions from coal-fired power plants in the U.S. and Canada is a significant market, and is served by the Company with its broad line of FLUEPAC&#xAE; powdered activated carbons.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s Rayox&#xAE; UV System is an industry staple for the destruction of groundwater pollutants, as well as for the removal of alcohol, phenol and acetone in process water and total organic compound (TOC) reduction in wastewater treatment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s Hyde GUARDIAN&#xAE; BWMS is a fully automated system that can be integrated into a ship&#x2019;s ballast control system.&nbsp;&nbsp;The compact design can be skid mounted for new construction or can be made modular for easy installation in crowded machinery spaces on existing vessels.&nbsp; It is capable of providing complete ballast water management solutions for a variety of vessels including cruise ships, cargo and container ships, offshore supply vessels, and military vessels.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Food and Beverage Market.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;In this market, sweetener manufacturers are principal purchasers of the Company&#x2019;s activated carbon products, and also use the Company&#x2019;s DE and perlite filtration media products.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s wood-based and coal-based activated carbon products are used in the purification of dextrose and high fructose corn syrup.&nbsp;&nbsp;Activated carbons are also sold for use in the purification of cane sugar.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s DE and perlite filtration media and high performing activated carbons are used in applications such as the wine, beer, and flavoring markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other food and beverage processing applications include de-colorization and purification of many different foods and beverages and for purifying water, liquids and gases prior to usage in brewing and bottling.&nbsp;&nbsp;Continuous ion-exchange systems are also used in this market for the production of lysine and vitamin E as well as purification of dextrose, high fructose corn syrup and sugar cane.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Specialty Market.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;The Company is a major supplier of specialty activated carbons to manufacturers of gas masks for the U.S. and European military as well as protective respirators and collective filters for first responders and private </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Sales and Marketing</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In the U.S., the Company operates primarily through a direct sales force.&nbsp;&nbsp;In some markets and regions, the Company also sells through agents and distributors.&nbsp;&nbsp;In Latin America and Canada, the Company maintains &nbsp;a sales office in Sao Paulo, Brazil, and sells through agent/distributor relationships.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">In the Asia Pacific Region, the Company maintains sales offices in Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, China; Hong Kong; Osaka, Japan; Tokyo, Japan; Singapore; and Taipei, Taiwan, and uses direct sales as well as agents and distributors.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">In Europe, the Company maintains sales offices in Feluy, Belgium; Kolding, Denmark; Paris, France; Beverungen, Germany; Milan, Italy; Ashton-in-Makerfield, United Kingdom; Houghton-le-Spring, United Kingdom; and Gothenburg, Sweden, and operates through a direct sales force.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also has a network of agents and distributors that conduct sales in certain countries in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">Many offices can play a role in sales of products or services from each of the Company&#x2019;s segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Geographic sales information can be found in Note 18 to the consolidated financial statements in Item 8 of this Annual Report.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also refer to Risk Factors in Item 1A.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company had a sales backlog of $10.1 million and $15.4 million as of January 31, 2017 and 2016, respectively, in the Equipment segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $5.3 million decrease was a result of regulatory delays for ballast water treatment systems and several large contracts that were completed during 2016 that more than offset new contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company expects to carry approximately $1.3 million of the 2017 backlog into 2018 and $0.5 million into 2019.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">With respect to the production and sale of activated carbon related products, the Company has a major global presence, and has several competitors in the worldwide market.&nbsp;&nbsp;Norit, a subsidiary of Cabot Corporation, Ingevity Corporation, formerly the Specialty Chemicals Division of WestRock Company, a U.S. company, Jacobi Carbons, a Swedish company, and Evoqua Water Technologies (formerly Siemens Water Technologies), a U.S. company, are the primary competitors.&nbsp;&nbsp;Chinese producers of coal-based activated carbon and certain East Asian producers of coconut-based activated carbon participate in the market on a worldwide basis and sell principally through numerous resellers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Competition in activated carbons, carbon equipment and services is based on quality, performance, and/or price.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other sources of competition for the Company&#x2019;s activated carbon services and systems are alternative technologies for purification, filtration, and extraction processes that do not employ activated carbons.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">A number of other smaller competitors engage in the production and sale of activated carbons and in local markets, but do not compete with the Company on a global basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;These companies compete with the Company in the sale of specific types of activated carbons, but do not generally compete with a broad range of products in the worldwide activated carbon business.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, ADA Carbon Solutions, owned by Energy Capital Partners, competes with the Company in the America&#x2019;s market for the removal of mercury from coal-fired power plant flue gas.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">With respect to the Company&#x2019;s DE and perlite filtration media products, due to their low weight, low density physical properties, the Company primarily distributes these products throughout the European region.&nbsp;&nbsp;Competitors in the region include EP Minerals, Imerys and Dicalite.&nbsp;&nbsp;Similar to activated carbon, competition for these products is primarily based on quality, performance and/or price.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s UV technologies product line has primary competition from Trojan Technologies, Inc., a Canadian company owned by Danaher Corporation, a U.S. company, and Xylem Inc, headquartered in White Plains, N.Y., a U.S. company.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The principal raw material purchased by the Company for its Activated Carbon and Service segment is bituminous coal from mines primarily in the U.S. purchased under long term and annual supply contracts, as well as spot purchases.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company purchases natural gas from various suppliers for use in its Activated Carbon and Service segment production facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;In both the U.S. and Europe, natural gas is purchased pursuant to various annual and multi-year contracts, as well as spot purchases.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company buys various metals, acids and other additives that are used within the activated carbon production process to enhance the performance of certain products.&nbsp;&nbsp;These materials are bought under multi-year and annual contracts, as well as on a spot basis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">The purchase of key equipment components and fabrications are coordinated through agreements with various suppliers for UV,&nbsp;ISEP&#xAE; and the carbon equipment markets.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">With the recent addition of the New Business, the Company also purchases wood from a local forest in Europe.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company owns two mineral deposit quarry sources, which provide raw materials for its DE manufacturing processes.&nbsp;&nbsp;These quarries each have 20 or more years of raw material reserves available.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company obtains its crude perlite oar raw material from mines located in the Mediterranean region.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s primary research and development (R&amp;D) activities are conducted at an innovation center in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania with an additional facility in Japan.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Pittsburgh facility is used for the evaluation of experimental activated carbon and equipment and application development.&nbsp;&nbsp;Experimental systems are also designed and evaluated at this location.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The principal goals of the R&amp;D&#x2019;s research program are to improve the Company&#x2019;s position as a technological leader in solving customers&#x2019; problems with its products, services and equipment; develop new products and services; and provide technical support to customers and operations of the Company. &nbsp; &nbsp;Research programs include new and improved methods for manufacturing and utilizing new and enhanced activated carbons.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company performs R&amp;D to continuously advance the application of UV technologies to pathogens as well as new and emerging contaminants.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, R&amp;D is devoted to continual product advancement for reduction of life cycle cost to the customer and to ensure compliance with U.S. and international regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;This includes R&amp;D work on Advanced Oxidation for treatment of taste and odor compounds (MIB and Geosmin), nitrosamines, pesticide/herbicides and pharmaceutical/personal care products.</font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Item 1A. Risk Factors:<a name="Item1ARiskFactors_208958"></a></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Risks relating to our business</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Increases in U.S. and European imports of Chinese or other foreign manufactured activated carbon could have an adverse effect on our financial results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We face pressure and competition in our U.S. and European markets from brokers of low cost imported activated carbon products, primarily from China.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe we offer the market technically superior products and related customer support.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, in some applications, low cost imports have become accepted as viable alternatives to our products because they have been frequently sold at less than fair value in the market.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the markets in which we compete experience an increase in these imported low cost carbons, especially if sold at less than fair value, we could see declines in net sales.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the sales of these low cost activated carbons may make it more difficult for us to pass through raw material price increases to our customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In response to a petition from the U.S. activated carbon industry filed in March&nbsp;2006, the U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce Department) announced the imposition of anti-dumping duties starting in October&nbsp;2006.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Commerce Department announcement was based on extensive economic analysis of the operations and pricing practices of the Chinese producers and exporters.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Commerce Department announcement required U.S. Customs and Border Protection to require importers of steam activated carbon from China to post a provisional bond or cash deposit in the amount of the duties.&nbsp;&nbsp;The anti-dumping duties are intended to offset the amount by which the steam activated carbon from China is sold at less than fair value in the U.S.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Annual reviews of duties begin to occur in April&nbsp;of the year following the twelve month period then completed.&nbsp;&nbsp;The significant anti-dumping duties originally imposed by the Commerce Department, and the affirmative decision by the International Trade Commission (ITC), has had an adverse impact on the cost of Chinese manufactured activated carbon imported into the U.S.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the anti-dumping duties could be further reduced or eliminated in the future which could adversely affect demand or pricing of our product.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">We have operations in multiple foreign countries and, as a result, are subject to foreign exchange translation risk, which could have an adverse effect on our financial results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We conduct significant business operations in several foreign countries.&nbsp;&nbsp;Of our 2016 net sales, approximately 47% were sales to customers outside of the U.S., and 2016 net sales denominated in non-U.S. dollars represented approximately 32% of our overall net sales.&nbsp; With the acquisition of the New Business, these percentages are expected to increase.&nbsp; We conduct business in the local currencies of each of our foreign subsidiaries or affiliates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those local currencies are then translated into U.S. dollars at the applicable exchange rates for inclusion in our consolidated financial statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The exchange rates between some of these currencies and the U.S. dollar in recent years have fluctuated significantly and may continue to do so in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in exchange rates, particularly the strengthening of the U.S. dollar, could significantly reduce our sales and profitability from foreign subsidiaries or affiliates from one period to the next as local currency amounts are translated into fewer U.S. dollars.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Our European and Japanese activated carbon businesses are sourced from both the U.S. and China, which subjects these businesses to foreign exchange transaction risk.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our virgin activated carbon is produced primarily in the U.S.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also source significant quantities of activated carbon in China.&nbsp;&nbsp;Produced and sourced activated carbons are provisioned to all of our global operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Purchases of these carbons are typically denominated in U.S. dollars yet are ultimately sold in other currencies thereby creating foreign currency exchange transaction risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;We generally execute foreign currency derivative contracts of not more than eighteen months in duration to cover a portion of our known or projected foreign currency exposure.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, those contracts do not protect us from longer-term trends of a strengthening U.S. dollar, which could significantly increase our cost of activated carbon delivered to our European and Japanese markets, and we may not be able to offset these costs by increasing our prices.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">12</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Our financial results could be adversely affected by an interruption of supply or an increase in the price of raw materials we use, such as coal and wood.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We use bituminous coal as the main raw material in our activated carbon production process.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon our current projected usage and price, we estimate that our 2017 coal costs in the U.S. will be approximately $26.6 million excluding the cost of transportation to our carbon manufacturing facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have various annual and multi-year contracts in place for the supply of our coal that expire at various intervals in 2017 and 2018 and cover approximately 88% of our expected 2017 tonnage.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interruptions in coal supply caused by mine accidents, labor disputes, transportation delays, breach of supplier contractual obligations, floods or other events for other than a temporary period could have an adverse effect on our ability to meet customer demand.&nbsp;&nbsp;We use very specific high quality metallurgical coals for many of our products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our inability to obtain these high-quality coals at competitive prices in a timely manner due to changing market conditions with limited high-quality suppliers could also have an adverse affect on our financial results.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, increases in the prices we pay for coal under our supply contracts could adversely affect our financial results by significantly increasing production costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon the current estimated usage and price of coal in 2017, a hypothetical 10% increase in the price of coal, excluding transportation costs, that is not covered by our supply contracts, would result in $0.5 million of additional pre-tax expense to us.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may not be able to pass through raw material price increases to our customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Additionally, as a result of our acquisition of the New Business in late 2016, wood has become an important raw material for us.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have various contracts in place to secure nearly half of our wood requirement through 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since we require a certain quality of wood, our inability to secure this product could affect our ability to meet customer demand for our products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our inability to obtain this quality at a reasonable price in a timely manner could affect our operations or financial position.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may not be able to pass through these raw material price increases to our customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">A planned or unplanned shutdown at one of our production facilities could have an adverse effect on our financial results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We operate multiple facilities and source product from strategic partners who operate facilities which are close to water or in areas susceptible to floods, hurricanes, and earthquakes.&nbsp;&nbsp;An unplanned shutdown at any of our or our strategic partners&#x2019; facilities for more than a temporary period as a result of a hurricane, typhoon, earthquake, flood or other natural disaster, or as a result of fire, explosions, war, terrorist activities, political conflict or other hostilities, or as a result of unforeseen mechanical problems, could significantly affect our ability to meet our demand requirements, thereby resulting in lost sales and profitability in the short-term or eventual loss of customers in the long term.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, a prolonged planned shutdown of any of our production facilities due to a change in the business conditions could result in impairment charges that could have an adverse impact on our financial results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Delays in enactment of new state or federal regulations could restrict our ability to reach our strategic growth targets and lower our return on invested capital.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our strategic growth initiatives are reliant upon more restrictive environmental regulations being enacted for the purpose of making water and air cleaner and safer.&nbsp;&nbsp;Examples include regulation of mercury emissions, drinking water disinfection by-products, and ship ballast water.&nbsp;&nbsp;If stricter regulations are delayed or are not enacted or enacted but subsequently repealed or amended to be less strict, or enacted with prolonged phase-in periods, our sales growth targets could be adversely affected and our return on invested capital could be reduced.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For example, our Hyde GUARDIAN&#xAE; ballast water treatment system received type approval from the IMO in April 2009.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the IMO Ballast Water Management Convention, which mandates the use of IMO approved ballast water treatment systems for ships in international traffic, was not ratified until September 2016 and is not scheduled to go into force until September 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Similarly, the USCG regulates ballast water in U.S. waters, and will not follow the IMO convention.&nbsp;&nbsp;We, along with several other ballast water treatment system manufacturers have received Alternate Management System designation from the USCG, but this is a temporary designation while full USCG type approval is pursued.&nbsp;&nbsp;In December 2015, the USCG decided it would not allow us, and several other manufacturers of ultraviolet light-based ballast water treatment systems, to use the Most Probable Number (MPN) test method for purposes of testing the Company&#x2019;s system to apply for type approval under USCG regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Consequently, we have redesigned our Hyde GUARDIAN&#xAE; system under USCG testing protocols and are embarking on testing to support our application for USCG Type Approval in the fourth quarter of 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The first USCG type approvals were granted to competitors in December 2016 and two of these approvals were for UV light-based systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;While we remain confident in our product&#x2019;s </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">13</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">capabilities, there can be no assurance that we will receive USCG type approval or that additional approval of competing systems will not have an adverse effect on the Company&#x2019;s ability to compete in the market for ballast water treatment systems for vessels discharging ballast water in U.S. waterways and ports.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Our required capital expenditures may exceed estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our capital expenditures were $31.9 million in 2016 and are forecasted to be approximately</font><font style="display:inline;color:#FF0000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">$70 million to $80 million in 2017, including capital expenditures related to the New Business.  Future capital expenditures may be significantly higher and may vary substantially if we are required to undertake certain actions to comply with new regulatory requirements or compete with new technologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may not have the capital to undertake the capital investments.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we are unable to do so, we may not be able to effectively compete.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As described in the Report of Management in "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data," we have concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was ineffective as of December 31, 2016 because a material weakness existed in our internal control over financial reporting related to the recognition of revenue for a subset of transactions within the U.S. potable water market. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Management has identified actions that the Company intends to implement immediately in order to remediate this material weakness. However, we have not completed all of the corrective actions that we believe are necessary.&nbsp;&nbsp;As we continue to evaluate and work to remediate the material weakness, we may implement additional measures.&nbsp;&nbsp;The actions we are taking to remediate the material weakness are subject to ongoing senior management review, as well as oversight by the Audit Committee of our Board of Directors.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">If our remedial measures are insufficient to address the material weakness, or if additional material weaknesses or significant deficiencies in our internal control over financial reporting are discovered or occur in the future, our consolidated financial statements may contain material misstatements and we could be required to restate our financial results, which could adversely affect our stock price and result in our inability to maintain compliance with applicable stock exchange listing requirements.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Riom-&#xE8;s-Montagnes plant occupies approximately 3 acres and is located in south-central France.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plant produces Clarcel&#xAE; brand diatomaceous earth which is mined from the diatomite quarry also acquired from CECA which is located in Viragues, France, approximately 23 miles from Riom-&#xE8;s-Montagnes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plant is approximately 30,000 square feet and the quarry is approximately 118 acres.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Saint Bauzile plant, located in Chomerac, France produces Clarcel&#xAE; brand diatomaceous earth which is mined from the diatomite quarry also acquired from CECA which is located in Saint-Bauzile, France.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plant occupies a 17 acre site, and is approximately 163,000 square feet.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Foggia, Italy plant produces Randalite&#xAE; and Randafil&#x2122; brands perlite filtration media and it is located in southern Italy.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plant occupies 8 acres and consists of approximately 353,000 square feet. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The San Peitro di Legnago plant, located in northern Italy, occupies approximately 5 acres.&nbsp;&nbsp;The primary operation at the plant, which consists of approximately 54,000 square feet, includes the reactivation of spent granular activated carbons.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Item 3. Legal Proceedings:<a name="Item3LegalProceedings_658788"></a></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company is involved in various legal proceedings, lawsuits and claims, including employment, product warranty and environmental matters of a nature considered normal to its business.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is the Company&#x2019;s policy to accrue for amounts related to the legal matters when it is probable that a liability has been incurred and the loss amount is reasonably estimable.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On February 21, 2017, the Japan Fair Trade Commission (the JFTC) informed the Company&#x2019;s subsidiary, Calgon Carbon Japan (CCJ) that it is investigating CCJ along with several other manufacturers and distributors that participate in the activated carbon market in Japan over concerns of anti-competitive conduct.&nbsp;&nbsp;The JFTC is investigating whether manufacturers and sellers of activated carbon used in water purification plants, garbage incineration plants and other similar facilities in Japan have acted in concert with each other in violation of the Japan Anti-Monopoly Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;JFTC agents searched the offices of CCJ, reviewing and collecting contracts and other business records and interviewed certain CCJ employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;At this early stage of the investigation, it is difficult to predict the outcome of this matter or what remedies, if any, may be imposed by the JFTC.&nbsp;&nbsp;CCJ is cooperating with the JFTC as it conducts its investigation.</font>
		</p>
