		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Property, Plant and Equipment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Property, plant and equipment is recorded at cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;Repair and maintenance costs are expensed as incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation for financial reporting purposes is computed on the straight-line method over the estimated service lives of the assets, which are from 15 to 30 years for land improvements and buildings, 5 to 15 years for furniture, machinery and equipment, 5 to 10 years for customer capital, 5 years for vehicles, and 5 to 10 years for computer hardware and software.&nbsp;&nbsp;Expenditures for new facilities and improvements that substantially extend the capacity or useful life of an asset are capitalized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Mineral rights were acquired as part of the acquisition of the New Business.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mineral rights include diatomite ore deposits, and are stated at cost, less accumulated depletion.&nbsp;&nbsp;Depletion is computed for mineral rights using the units-of-production method and is included in the Company&#x2019;s depreciation expense.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Asset Retirement Obligations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As a result of the acquisition of the New Business, the Company has recognized asset retirement obligations (AROs) related to reclamation obligations associated with the normal operation of the diatomite mining facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;These AROs consist primarily of costs associated with mine reclamation and landfill closures.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair values of these AROs are recorded on a discounted basis at the time the obligation is incurred, and accreted over time for the change in present value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the Company capitalizes asset retirement costs by increasing the carrying amount of the related long-lived assets and depreciating these assets over the remaining life of the active mining facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company reviews, on an annual basis, unless otherwise deemed necessary, the reclamation obligation at each active mine site in accordance with accounting guidance for reclamation obligations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Goodwill represents the excess of the cost of an acquired business over the fair value of the identifiable tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed in a business combination.&nbsp;&nbsp;Identifiable intangible assets acquired in business combinations are recorded based on their fair values at the date of acquisition.&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with guidance within Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 350 &#x201C;Intangibles - Goodwill and Other&#x201D; goodwill and identifiable intangible assets with indefinite lives are not subject to amortization but must be evaluated for impairment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As a result of the acquisition of the New Business, the Company has recorded various intangible assets, including trade names and trademarks, unpatented technology, and customer relationships.&nbsp;&nbsp;The trade names and trademarks acquired have indefinite lives and will be tested for impairment annually.&nbsp;&nbsp;All remaining acquired identifiable intangible assets have finite lives.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company evaluates goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment annually, or when events occur or circumstances change that may reduce the fair value of the asset below its carrying amount.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has elected to perform the annual impairment test of its goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets, as required, on December&nbsp;31 of each year by initially comparing the fair value of each of the Company&#x2019;s reporting units to their related carrying values.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the fair value of the reporting unit is less than its carrying value, the Company performs an additional step to determine the implied fair value of the goodwill.&nbsp;&nbsp;The implied fair value of goodwill is determined by first allocating the fair value of the reporting unit to all of the assets and liabilities of the unit and then computing the excess of the unit&#x2019;s fair value over the amounts assigned to the assets and liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the carrying value of goodwill exceeds the implied fair value of goodwill, such excess represents the amount of goodwill impairment, and the Company recognizes such impairment accordingly.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair values are estimated using discounted cash flows and other valuation methodologies that are based on projections of the amounts and timing of future revenues and cash flows, assumed discount rates and other </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">53</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">assumptions as deemed appropriate.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also considers such factors as historical performance, anticipated market conditions, operating expense trends and capital expenditure requirements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s identifiable intangible assets other than goodwill and trade names and trademarks have finite lives.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain of these intangible assets, such as customer relationships, are amortized using an accelerated methodology while others, such as patents, are amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, intangible assets with finite lives are evaluated for impairment whenever events or circumstances indicate that their carrying amount may not be recoverable, as prescribed by guidance within ASC 360 &#x201C;Property, Plant, and Equipment.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Long-Lived Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company evaluates long-lived assets under the provisions of ASC 360 &#x201C;Property, Plant, and Equipment&#x201D; which addresses financial accounting and reporting for the impairment of long-lived assets and for long-lived assets to be disposed of.&nbsp;&nbsp;For assets to be held and used, the Company groups a long-lived asset or assets with other assets and liabilities at the lowest level for which identifiable cash flows are largely independent of the cash flows of other assets and liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;An impairment loss for an asset group reduces only the carrying amounts of a long-lived asset or assets of the group being evaluated.&nbsp;&nbsp;The loss is allocated to the long-lived assets of the group on a pro-rata basis using the relative carrying amounts of those assets, except that the loss allocated to an individual long-lived asset of the group does not reduce the carrying amount of that asset below its fair value whenever that fair value is determinable without undue cost and effort.&nbsp;&nbsp;Estimates of future cash flows to test the recoverability of a long-lived asset group include only the future cash flows that are directly associated with and that are expected to arise as a direct result of the use and eventual disposition of the asset group.&nbsp;&nbsp;The future cash flow estimates used by the Company exclude interest charges.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value hierarchy distinguishes between (1) market participant assumptions developed based on market data obtained from independent sources (observable inputs) and (2) an entity&#x2019;s own assumptions about market participant assumptions developed based on the best information available in the circumstances (unobservable inputs).&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value hierarchy consists of three broad levels, which gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1) and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs (Level 3).&nbsp;&nbsp;The three levels of the fair value hierarchy are described below:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Level 1 &#x2014; Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Level 2 &#x2014; Inputs, other than the quoted prices in active markets, that are observable either directly or indirectly; and</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Level 3 &#x2014; Unobservable inputs that reflect the reporting entity&#x2019;s own assumptions.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s financial instruments, excluding derivative instruments, consist primarily of cash and cash equivalents, short and long-term debt as well as accounts receivable and accounts payable.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of accounts receivable and accounts payable approximates their carrying value because of the short-term maturity of the instruments. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Derivative Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company applies ASC 815 &#x201C;Derivatives and Hedging&#x201D; which establishes accounting and reporting standards for derivative instruments, including certain derivative instruments embedded in other contracts and for hedging activities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Derivative financial instruments are utilized by the Company to manage risk exposure to movements in foreign exchange rates or the prices of natural gas.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company enters into derivative financial instruments with high credit quality counterparties and diversifies its positions among such counterparties.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, various master netting arrangements are in place with counterparties to facilitate settlement of gains and losses on these contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;The </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">54</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">Company does not net its derivative positions by counterparty for purposes of balance sheet presentation and disclosure.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in the value of the derivative financial instruments are measured at the balance sheet date and recognized in current earnings or other comprehensive income depending on whether the derivative is designated as part of a hedge transaction and meets certain other criteria.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not hold derivative financial instruments for trading purposes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Pensions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company accounts for its pensions in accordance with ASC 715 &#x201C;Compensation &#x2013; Retirement Benefits.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounting for pensions involves estimating the cost of benefits to be provided well into the future and attributing that cost over the time period each employee works.&nbsp;&nbsp;To accomplish this, extensive use is made of assumptions about inflation, investment returns, mortality, turnover and discount rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;These assumptions are reviewed annually.&nbsp;&nbsp;In determining the expected return on plan assets, the Company evaluates long-term actual return information, the mix of investments that comprise plan assets and future estimates of long-term investment returns.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company uses country specific mortality tables and updates them periodically as better information becomes available.&nbsp;&nbsp;In determining the discount rates for pension obligations, the Company evaluates long-term corporate bonds that receive one of the two highest ratings given by a recognized rating agency.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Amortization of the actuarial net gain or loss as a result of experience differing from that assumed and from changes in assumptions is included as a component of net periodic pension cost for the year.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company uses a 10% corridor such that if, as of the beginning of the year, the net gain or loss exceeds 10% of the greater of the projected benefit obligation or the market-related value of plan assets, the amortization is that excess divided by the average future working lifetime of participating employees expected to receive benefits under the plan or the average remaining life expectancy of the plan&#x2019;s participants if the percentage of actives is less than 10% of the total population.&nbsp;&nbsp;As only the excess actuarial gain or loss is amortized, this approach will not fully amortize the net actuarial gain or loss.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Stock-Based Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company applies ASC 718 &#x201C;Compensation &#x2014; Stock Compensation.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with guidance within ASC 718, compensation expense for stock options is recorded over the vesting period using the fair value on the date of grant, as calculated by the Company using the Black-Scholes model.&nbsp;&nbsp;For time vested restricted stock awards, the nonvested restricted stock grant date fair value, which is the market price of the underlying common stock, is expensed over the vesting period.&nbsp;&nbsp;For certain performance based stock awards, the initial grant date fair value of the performance stock awards that vest subject to a market condition is determined using a Monte Carlo simulation model and is expensed on a straight-line basis over the performance period.&nbsp;&nbsp;For certain performance based stock awards that vest subject to a performance condition, the initial grant date fair value is the market price of the underlying common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;This fair value is expensed on a straight-line basis over the performance period when it is probable that the performance condition will be achieved.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s stock-based compensation plans are more fully described in Note 10.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Net Income per Common Share</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Basic net income per common share is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Diluted net income per common share is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding plus all potential dilutive common shares outstanding during the period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Potential dilutive common shares are determined using the treasury stock method.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the treasury stock method, exercise of options is assumed at the beginning of the period when the average stock price during the period exceeds the exercise price of outstanding options and common shares are assumed issued.&nbsp;&nbsp;The proceeds from exercise are assumed to be used to purchase common stock at the average market price during the period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The incremental shares to be issued are considered to be the potential dilutive common shares outstanding.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">55</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences of temporary differences between the book and tax basis of assets and liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;If it is more likely than not that some portion or all of a deferred tax asset will not be realized, a valuation allowance is recognized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company assesses its ability to realize deferred tax assets based on normalized historical performance and on projections of future taxable income in the relevant tax jurisdictions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Normalized historical performance for purposes of this assessment includes adjustments for those income and expense items that are unusual and non-recurring in nature and are not expected to affect results in future periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such unusual and non-recurring items include the effects of legal fees or settlements associated with specific litigation matters, acquisition and restructuring costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s projections of future taxable income considers known events, such as the passage of legislation or expected occurrences, and do not reflect a general growth assumption.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s estimates of future taxable income are reviewed annually or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that such projections should be modified.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company utilizes guidance within ASC 740 &#x201C;Income Taxes&#x201D; regarding the accounting for uncertainty in income taxes.&nbsp;&nbsp;This guidance prescribes recognition and measurement standards for a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return.&nbsp;&nbsp;According to this guidance, the evaluation of a tax position is a two step process.&nbsp;&nbsp;The first step is the determination of whether a tax position should be recognized in the financial statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The benefit of a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return is to be recognized only if the Company determines that it is more likely than not that the tax position will be sustained upon examination by the tax authorities based upon the technical merits of the position.&nbsp;&nbsp;In step two, for those tax positions which should be recognized, the measurement of a tax position is determined as being the largest amount of benefit that is greater than 50% likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">No provision is made for U.S. income taxes on the undistributed earnings of non-U.S. subsidiaries because these earnings are intended to be indefinitely reinvested outside the U.S.&nbsp;&nbsp;These earnings would become subject to income tax if they were remitted as dividends, were loaned to the Company or a U.S. affiliate, or if the Company were to sell its ownership interest in the subsidiaries. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In November 2015, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) 2015-17, &#x201C;Balance Sheet Classification of Deferred Taxes&#x201D; which requires that all deferred tax assets (DTAs) and deferred tax liabilities (DTLs), along with any related valuation allowance, be classified as noncurrent in a classified balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;Netting of DTAs and DTLs by tax jurisdiction is still required under the new guidance.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company adopted ASU 2015-17 effective December 31, 2016 on a prospective basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Adoption of this ASU resulted in an initial reclassification of $18.1 million of the Company&#x2019;s net current deferred income tax asset to the long-term deferred income tax asset in its consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to required netting by tax jurisdiction, a large portion of this amount was netted against the long-term deferred income tax liability.&nbsp;&nbsp;No prior periods were retrospectively adjusted.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Leases</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company leases certain facilities, equipment and vehicles.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain of the Company&#x2019;s leases contain renewal options, rent escalation clauses and landlord incentives.&nbsp;&nbsp;Renewal terms generally reflect market rates at the time of renewal.&nbsp;&nbsp;Rent expense for noncancelable operating leases with scheduled rent increases or landlord incentives is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term, including any applicable rent holidays, beginning with the lease commencement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;The excess of straight-line rent expense over scheduled payment amounts and landlord incentives is recorded as a deferred liability. &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Contingencies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company from time to time is subject to various legal proceedings, lawsuits and claims, including employment, product warranty and environmental matters of the nature considered normal to its business.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is the Company&#x2019;s policy to accrue for amounts related to legal matters when it is probable that a liability has been incurred and the loss amount is reasonably estimable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Estimates are developed through consultation with legal counsel involved in the defense and are based upon an analysis of probable results, assuming a combination of litigation and settlement strategies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Legal fees associated with defending these various lawsuits and claims are expensed when incurred.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Government Grants</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s policy for accounting for government grants, including non-monetary grants at fair value, is to recognize them only when there is reasonable assurance that (a) the Company will comply with the conditions attached to the grants and (b) the grants will be received.&nbsp;&nbsp;A grant will be recognized over the period necessary to match it to the related costs, for which it is intended to compensate, on a systematic basis.&nbsp; A grant related to assets is presented by deducting it from the asset&#x2019;s carrying amount and is reported within cash flows from investing activities.&nbsp;&nbsp;A grant related to income will be deducted from the related expense and reported within cash flows from operating activities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Labor Agreements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Collective bargaining agreements cover approximately 46% of the Company&#x2019;s full-time labor force as of December 31, 2016 that expire at various dates through 2019.&nbsp; Approximately 6% of the Company&#x2019;s labor force is operating under contracts that expired on December 31, 2016, which are in the process of being renegotiated.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">New Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-09, &#x201C;Revenue (Topic 606): Revenue from Contracts with Customers&#x201D; which outlines a single comprehensive model for entities to use in accounting for revenue arising from contracts with customers and supersedes most current revenue recognition guidance, including industry-specific guidance.&nbsp;&nbsp;The core principle of ASU 2014-09 is that an entity should recognize revenue when it transfers promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services by applying five steps listed in the guidance.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2014-09 also requires disclosure of both quantitative and qualitative information that enables users of financial statements to understand the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows arising from customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;In August 2015, the FASB issued ASU 2015-14, which defers the effective date of ASU 2014-09 by one year.&nbsp;&nbsp;In March 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-08, &#x201C;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606):&nbsp;&nbsp;Principal versus Agent Considerations (Reporting Revenue Gross versus Net)&#x201D; which amends the principal-versus agent implementation guidance and illustrations in FASB&#x2019;s new revenue standard ASU 2014-09.&nbsp;&nbsp;The new guidance includes indicators to assist an entity in determining whether it controls a specified good or service before it is transferred to the customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;In April 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-10, &#x201C;Identifying Performance Obligations and Licensing&#x201D; which amends certain aspects of the guidance in ASU 2014-09.&nbsp;&nbsp;For identifying performance obligations, the amendments include:&nbsp;&nbsp;immaterial promised goods and services, shipping and handling activities, and identifying when promises represent performance obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;In May 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-12, &#x201C;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606):&nbsp;&nbsp;Narrow-Scope Improvements and Practical Expedients.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;This clarifies the collectability assessment, sales tax presentation and the treatment of contract modifications and completed contracts at transition.&nbsp;&nbsp;In May 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-11, &#x201C;Rescission of SEC Guidance Because of Accounting Standards Update 2014-09&#x201D; which rescinds certain SEC guidance upon adoption including those related to freight services in process and shipping and handling fees.&nbsp;&nbsp;All of the new guidance is effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December 15, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is currently determining the potential impacts of the new standard on its contract portfolio.&nbsp;&nbsp;The approach includes performing a detailed review of key contracts representative of its different businesses and comparing historical accounting policies and practices to the new standard.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company will continue to evaluate the provisions of this ASU to assess the </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">57</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">impact it may have on its consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is planning to adopt the provisions of the ASU and its subsequent amendments using the modified retrospective transition method for existing transactions that may result in a cumulative effect adjustment as of January 1, 2018.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In July 2015, the FASB issued ASU 2015-11, &#x201C;Simplifying the Measurement of Inventory&#x201D; which requires entities to measure most inventory at the lower of cost and net realizable value.&nbsp;&nbsp;This simplifies the current guidance under which an entity measures inventory at the lower of cost or market.&nbsp;&nbsp;Market in this context is defined as one of three different measures, one of which is net realizable value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net realizable value is the estimated selling prices in the ordinary course of business, less reasonably predictable costs of completion, disposal, and transportation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The new guidance will be applied prospectively, and is effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December 15, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The adoption of this ASU is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-02, &#x201C;Leases (Topic 842)&#x201D; which introduces a lessee model that brings most leases on the balance sheet, requiring lessees to recognize the right to use assets and lease obligations that arise from lease arrangements exceeding a twelve month term.&nbsp;&nbsp;Lessees will also need to disclose qualitative and quantitative information about lease transactions, such as information about variable lease payments and options to renew and terminate leases.&nbsp;&nbsp;For income statement purposes, the FASB retained a dual model, requiring leases to be classified as either operating or finance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Classification will be based on criteria that are largely similar to those applied in current lease accounting, but without explicit bright lines.&nbsp;&nbsp;Lessor accounting is similar to the current model, but updated to align with certain changes to the lessee model and the new revenue recognition standard.&nbsp;&nbsp;The new guidance is effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December 15, 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;Entities are required to use a modified retrospective transition for existing leases.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is evaluating the provisions of this ASU and assessing the impact it may have on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.&nbsp;&nbsp;At a minimum, total assets and total liabilities will increase in the period the ASU is adopted.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2016, the Company&#x2019;s undiscounted future minimum payments outstanding for lease obligations were approximately $41 million.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In March 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-09, &#x201C;Compensation &#x2013; Stock Compensation (Topic 718):&nbsp;&nbsp;Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting&#x201D; which simplifies several aspects of the accounting for employee share-based payment transactions, including the accounting for income taxes, forfeitures, and statutory tax withholding requirements, as well as classification in the statement of cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;The new guidance is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2016, including interim periods within those annual reporting periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is planning to adopt the provisions of this ASU using the modified retrospective transition method for existing share-based payment transactions, effective January 1, 2017.&nbsp; The adoption of this ASU is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In June 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-13, &#x201C;Financial Instruments &#x2013; Credit Losses (Topic 326):&nbsp;&nbsp;Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments&#x201D; which adds a Current Expected Credit Loss (CECL) model that is based on expected losses rather than incurred losses, which is applicable to trade receivables.&nbsp;&nbsp;The new guidance is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2019, including interim periods within those annual reporting periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Entities are required to use the modified retrospective approach.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is evaluating the provisions of this ASU and assessing the impact it may have on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In August and November 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-15, &#x201C;Statement of Cash Flows (Topic 230):&nbsp;&nbsp;Classification of Certain Cash Receipts and Cash Payments&#x201D; and ASU 2016-18, &#x201C;Statement of Cash Flows (Topic 230):&nbsp;&nbsp;Restricted Cash&#x201D; to add or clarify guidance on the classification of certain cash receipts and payments and restricted cash in the statement of cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;The new guidance is effective for annual reporting period beginning after December 15, 2017, including interim periods within those annual reporting periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Entities must apply the guidance retrospectively to all periods presented, but may apply it prospectively from the earliest date practicable if retrospective application would be </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">58</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">impracticable.&nbsp;&nbsp;The adoption of this ASU is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has elected to perform the annual impairment test of its goodwill, as required, on December&nbsp;31 of each year.&nbsp;&nbsp;For purposes of the test, the Company had historically identified six reporting units as defined within ASC 350 &#x201C;Intangibles &#x2013; Goodwill and Other&#x201D; at a regional level for the Activated Carbon and Service segment and at the technology level for the Equipment segment and has allocated goodwill to these reporting units accordingly.&nbsp;&nbsp;These reporting units consist of the Activated Carbon and Service segment which is segregated into two regional reporting units, the Americas/Asia and Europe, the Equipment segment which is segregated by technology (a) carbon adsorption, (b) ultraviolet light, and (c) ion exchange, and the Consumer segment which includes the charcoal cloth reporting unit.&nbsp;&nbsp;The goodwill associated with the Consumer segment is not material and has not been allocated below the segment level.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Accounts receivable and accounts payable included in the consolidated balance sheets approximate fair value and are excluded from the table above.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of cash and cash equivalents are based on quoted prices.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of derivative assets and liabilities are measured based on inputs from market sources that aggregate data based upon market transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value for the acquisition earn-out liability is based upon Level 2 inputs which are periodically re-evaluated for changes in future projections and the discount rate.&nbsp;&nbsp;This liability is recorded in accrued pension and other liabilities within the Company&#x2019;s consolidated balance sheets. &nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s debt bears interest based on market rates and, accordingly, the carrying value of this obligation approximates fair value.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">6. Derivative Instruments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company uses foreign currency forward exchange contracts and foreign exchange option contracts to limit the exposure of exchange rate fluctuations on certain foreign currency receivables, payables, and other known and forecasted transactional exposures for periods consistent with the expected cash flow of the underlying transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management&#x2019;s policy for managing foreign currency risk is to use derivatives to hedge up to 75% of the value of the forecasted exposure.&nbsp;&nbsp;The foreign currency forward exchange and foreign exchange option contracts generally mature within eighteen months and are designed to limit exposure to exchange rate fluctuations.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company also uses natural gas forward contracts to limit the exposure to changes in natural gas prices.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management&#x2019;s policy for managing natural gas exposure is to use derivatives to hedge up to 75% of the forecasted natural gas requirements that are not fixed.&nbsp;&nbsp;The natural gas forward contracts generally mature within twenty-four months.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">61</font>

		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s hedging associated with foreign exchange contracts increased significantly as of December 31, 2016 as a result of an intercompany loan relating to the acquisition of the New Business. &nbsp;Related to these non-designated contracts, there was a net $4.4 million gain recognized for the year ended December 31, 2016, of which $5.7 million was realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The net gain was offset by a foreign exchange unrealized transaction loss of $5.0 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amounts are recorded in earnings, in other expense &#x2013; net.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The use of derivatives exposes the Company to the risk that a counterparty may default on a derivative contract.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company enters into derivative financial instruments with high credit quality counterparties and diversifies its positions among such counterparties.&nbsp;&nbsp;The aggregate fair value of the Company&#x2019;s derivative instruments in asset positions </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Derivatives in Cash Flow Hedging Relationships</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For derivative instruments that are designated and qualify as cash flow hedges, the effective portion of the gain or loss on the derivative is reported as a component of other comprehensive income (loss) (OCI) and reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods during which the hedged transaction affects earnings.&nbsp;&nbsp;The location of the gain or (loss) reclassified into earnings (effective portion) for derivatives in cash flow hedging relationships is cost of products sold (excluding depreciation and amortization).</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Upon entering into the Amended Credit Agreement, the Company incurred issuance costs of $0.8 million of which approximately $0.1&nbsp;million were expensed and the remainder were deferred and are being amortized over the term of the Amended Revolver and Term Loan facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;A quarterly nonrefundable commitment fee is payable by the Company based on the unused availability under the Amended Revolver and was equal to 0.23% as of December 31, 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The interest rate on amounts owed under the Amended Revolver and Term Loan will be, at the Company&#x2019;s option, either (i) a fluctuating Base Rate or (ii) an adjusted LIBOR rate plus in each case, an applicable margin based on the Company&#x2019;s leverage ratio as set forth in the Amended Credit Agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate charged on amounts owed under swing loans will be either (i) a fluctuating Base Rate or (ii) such other interest rates as the lender and the Company may agree to from time to time.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interest rate per annum on outstanding borrowings ranged from 2.51% to 2.62% as of December 31, 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company borrowed the full $100 million under the Term Loan on October 4, 2016 and repaid all amounts owed under the Credit Agreement. &nbsp;During the fourth quarter of 2016, the Company borrowed $160 million under the Amended Revolver to finance the acquisition of the New Business. &nbsp;&nbsp;Beginning January 1, 2017, the Company will be required to make quarterly repayments under the Term Loan equal to 1.25% of the outstanding balance until January 1, 2019, at which time the quarterly repayments will increase to 2.0% until the remaining balance is due on the October 4, 2023 maturity date.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, $5.0 million is shown as current portion of long-term debt within the consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2016.</font>

		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">Total outstanding borrowings and availability under the Amended Revolver as of December 31, 2016 were $125.0 million and $172.5 million respectively, after considering borrowings and outstanding letters of credit of $2.5 million. &nbsp;Total outstanding borrowings under the Term Loan were $100 million and there was no remaining availability as of December 31, 2016. &nbsp;Borrowings and repayments are presented on a gross basis within the Company&#x2019;s consolidated statement of cash flows.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Certain domestic subsidiaries of the Company unconditionally guarantee all indebtedness and obligations related to borrowings under the Amended Credit Agreement. &nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s obligations under the Amended Credit Agreement are unsecured.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Amended Credit Agreement contains customary affirmative and negative covenants for credit facilities of this type.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is permitted to pay dividends so long as the sum of availability under the Amended Credit Agreement and the amount of U.S. cash on hand is at least $50.0 million, and debt is less than or equal to 2.75x earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Amended Credit Agreement includes limitations on the Company and its subsidiaries with respect to indebtedness, additional liens, disposition of assets or subsidiaries, and transactions with affiliates.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company must comply with certain financial covenants including a minimum interest coverage ratio and a maximum leverage ratio as defined within the Credit Agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company was in compliance with all such covenants as of December 31, 2016. &nbsp;The Credit Agreement also provides for customary events of default, including failure to pay principal or interest when due, breach of representations and warranties, certain insolvency or receivership events affecting the Company and its subsidiaries and a change in control of the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;If an event of default occurs, the lenders would be under no further obligation to make loans or issue letters of credit.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon the occurrence of certain events of default, all outstanding obligations of the Company automatically would become immediately due and payable, and other events of default would allow the agent to declare all or any portion of the outstanding obligations of the Company to be immediately due and payable.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">9. Employee Benefit Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company sponsors defined benefit pension plans covering certain union and non-union employees in the U.S. and Europe.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2016, all of the U.S. plans are closed to new hires.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, future benefit accruals are frozen for a number of the plans.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company uses a measurement date of December 31 for all of its pension plans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During 2016, the Company offered certain eligible terminated vested participants in the U.S. pension plans the opportunity to elect a lump sum payment of their respective pension benefits. &nbsp;As a result of these elections, and significant lump sum payouts in the European plans, the Company paid benefits of $5.2 million, and incurred a &nbsp;settlement charge of $1.5 million in 2016. &nbsp;&nbsp;In 2015, the Company incurred settlement charges in both the U.S. and European plans that totaled $0.8 million as a result of employee retirements, and paid $3.8 million from plan assets.  In 2014, the Company offered certain eligible terminated vested participants in the U.S. pension plans the opportunity to elect a lump sum payment of their respective pension benefits, and as a result, incurred a settlement charge of $1.0 million and paid benefits of $4.4 million.&nbsp; As a result of the acquisition of the New Business, the projected benefit obligation of the European plans increased $3.9 million in 2016. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In 2014, the Society of Actuaries released a new mortality table &#x2013; RP-2014, and a new projection scale &#x2013; MP-2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company adopted the new RP-2014 mortality table and a modified version of the new MP-2014 projection scale for the U.S. plans as of December 31, 2014. &nbsp;The Company has continued to use the same mortality tables and the modified version of the projection scale in 2015 and 2016. &nbsp; &nbsp;For the European defined benefit plans, the Company utilizes country-specific mortality tables and has used the same tables for the majority of its European plans since 2014. &nbsp;In 2016, the Company updated the mortality tables used for the United Kingdom plans which did not cause a significant increase to the projected benefit obligations for those plans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The discount rates that the Company utilizes to determine pension obligations for its U.S. plans are based on a review of long-term corporate bonds that receive one of the two highest ratings given by a recognized rating agency.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The expected rate of return on plan assets was determined by the Company based on a review of asset class return expectations, as well as long-term inflation assumptions.&nbsp; Projected returns are based on broad equity and bond indices that the Company uses to benchmark its actual asset portfolio performance.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also considered historical returns on asset classes and investment mix. &nbsp;The expected long-term return on the U.S. plans&#x2019; assets is based on an asset allocation assumption of approximately 40%-50% equity securities, 45%-55% fixed income securities, and 5% with other investments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The expected long-term return on the European plans&#x2019; assets is based on its targeted portfolio mix of approximately 20%-30% equity securities, 55%-65% fixed income securities and 10%-20% other investments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also takes into account the effect on its projected returns from any reasonably likely changes in its asset portfolio when applicable. &nbsp; &nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s investment strategy is to earn the highest possible long-term total rate of return while minimizing the associated risk to ensure the preservation of the plan assets for the provision of benefits to participants and their beneficiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;This is accomplished by managing a diversified portfolio of fund styles, asset types, risk characteristics and investment holdings.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Multi-Employer Pension Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In addition to the aforementioned European plans, the Company participates in a multi-employer pension plan in Europe.&nbsp;&nbsp;This multi-employer plan almost entirely relates to former employees of operations it has divested.&nbsp;&nbsp;Benefits are distributed by the multi-employer plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of both December 31, 2016 and 2015, the Company had a&nbsp;$0.9 million liability recorded as a component of payroll and benefits payable within its consolidated balance sheets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Refer to Note 16 for further information related to this multi-employer plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Defined Contribution Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company sponsors a defined contribution plan for certain U.S. employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plan allows for employee contributions, and the Company can make fixed, matching and discretionary contributions to the plan on behalf of its employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also makes contributions to the USW 401(k) Plan for certain eligible employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total expenses related to the defined contribution plans were $3.8 million, $3.1 million, and $2.8 million for the years ended December 31, 2016, 2015, and 2014, respectively.</font>
		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">10. Stock Compensation Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In 2008, the Company adopted an equity incentive plan for eligible employees, service providers, and non-employee directors of the Company and its subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2014, the Company amended and restated the 2008 Equity Incentive Plan to increase the aggregate number of shares available for issuance from 2,000,000 to 5,000,000, and to extend the term for a period of ten years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plan includes a 1,500,000 share fixed sub-limit for the granting of incentive stock options.&nbsp;&nbsp;The awards may be stock options, restricted stock units, performance units or other stock-based awards.&nbsp;&nbsp;Stock options may be non-statutory or incentive.&nbsp;&nbsp;The exercise price for options and stock appreciation rights shall not be less than the fair market value on the date of grant, except if an incentive stock option is granted to a &#x201C;10% employee,&#x201D; as defined by the plan, then the option price may not be less than 110% of such fair market value. &nbsp;Options and stock&nbsp;appreciation rights may be exercisable commencing with the grant date, and are no longer exercisable after the expiration of seven or ten years from the grant date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The former Employee Stock Option Plan and the Non-Employee Directors&#x2019; Stock Option Plan (Prior Plans) were terminated and superseded by the 2008 Equity Incentive Plan. &nbsp;The Prior Plans both had stock-based awards outstanding as of December 31, 2016 and 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Prior Plans granted stock options and restricted stock to officers, directors and other key employees of the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;The stock options were granted at the fair market value on the grant date, became exercisable no less than six months after granted, and, in general, expire ten years after the date of grant.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Stock Options</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The expected dividend yield is based on the latest annualized dividend rate and the current market price of the underlying common stock at the date of grant. &nbsp;The expected volatility is based on the historical volatility of the Company&#x2019;s stock and the implied volatility calculated from traded options on the Company&#x2019;s stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risk-free interest rates are based on the U.S. Treasury strip rate for the expected life of the option. &nbsp; &nbsp;For the 2011 through 2016 grants of stock options, the Company used the simplified method for determining the expected life.&nbsp;&nbsp;This method was used since the Company granted stock options to a different population of its employees, and decreased the term from 10 to 7 years.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of these changes, the Company does not believe that the historical stock option exercise data provides a reasonable basis upon which to estimate the expected life for the 2011 through 2016 grants.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The total grant date fair value of options vested during the years ended December 31, 2016, 2015, and 2014 was $3.75 per share, $4.49 per share, and $4.80 per share, or $1.5 million, $1.5 million, and $1.3 million, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During the years ended December 31, 2016, 2015 and 2014, the total intrinsic value of stock options exercised (i.e., the difference between the market price at exercise and the price paid by the employee or non-employee directors to exercise the option) was $0.2 million, $0.4 million, and $1.0 million, respectively. &nbsp;The total amount of cash received from the exercise of options was $0.3 million, $1.1 million, and $2.2 million, for the years ended December 31, 2016, 2015, and 2014, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Restricted and Performance Based Stock Awards</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The grant date fair value of time vested restricted stock awards is the market price of the underlying common stock and is expensed over the vesting period of three years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Performance stock awards, based on Return on Capital (ROC), vest subject to the satisfaction of this performance condition, at the end of a three-year performance period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s actual ROC for the performance period is compared to the target set, and the actual award payout is interpolated.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ROC award can vest at between zero and 200 percent of the target award.&nbsp;&nbsp;The grant date fair value of the ROC performance stock is the market price of the underlying common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value is expensed on a straight-line basis over the performance period when it is probable that the performance condition will be achieved. &nbsp;No expense was recognized for these awards in 2016, 2015, or 2014 as it was not considered probable that the performance condition would be achieved.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Performance stock awards, based on Total Stockholder Return (TSR), vest subject to the satisfaction of this market condition, at the end of a three-year performance period.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s actual TSR for the performance period is compared to the results of its peer companies for the same period with the Company&#x2019;s relative position in the group determined by percentile rank.&nbsp;&nbsp;The actual award payout is determined by multiplying the target award by the performance factor percentage based upon the Company&#x2019;s percentile ranking and can vest at between zero and 200 percent of the target award.&nbsp;&nbsp;The initial grant date fair value of the TSR performance stock is determined using a Monte Carlo simulation model.&nbsp;&nbsp;The grant date fair value is expensed on a straight-line basis over the three-year performance period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">In February, 2015, the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors reinstated its common stock dividend program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Quarterly dividends of $0.05 per share were declared in each of the four quarters for the years ended December 31, 2016 and 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, in February, 2017, a common stock dividend of $0.05 per share was declared.&nbsp; No common stock dividends were declared during the year ended December 31, 2014.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In December&nbsp;2013, the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors approved a share repurchase program with a total of $150 million of purchases authorized.&nbsp;&nbsp;During 2014, the Company repurchased 1,930,841 shares at an average price of $20.57 per share. &nbsp;During 2015, the Company repurchased 2,002,444 shares at an average price of $17.45 per share.&nbsp;&nbsp;During 2016, the Company repurchased an additional 518,576 shares at an average price of $15.81 per share.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 2016, the Company had repurchased a total of 4,598,661 shares at an average price of $18.67 per share under the program.&nbsp;&nbsp;All of the above mentioned repurchases were funded from operating cash flows, cash on hand, and borrowings and the shares are held as treasury stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to these repurchases, the Company&#x2019;s remaining authorization to repurchase its common stock is approximately $64.1 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;In April 2016, the Company suspended the activities of the share repurchase program.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December 31, 2013, the Company had repurchased approximately 2.9 million common stock shares under an accelerated share repurchase program.&nbsp;&nbsp;These repurchases and some employee stock plan activity were inadvertently reflected as a reduction of the total common stock shares issued&nbsp;at that time.&nbsp;&nbsp;The number of common stock shares issued as of December 31, 2013 has been increased to adjust for this.&nbsp;&nbsp;This has also resulted in an increase in the common stock balance reported on the Company&#x2019;s financial statements as of December 31, 2013 of approximately $37 thousand, with a corresponding decrease to additional paid in capital.&nbsp; There is no impact to historically reported net income or earnings per share.</font>
